fixture_root.question: C1: does the module's own fixture root under CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE already exist, so that no /src mount is needed?
fixture_root.answer: No tree has to pre-exist under CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE, and no /src mount is needed. The runner only has to name an owned directory (the arm below minted an empty one with tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cwi-')); from that empty root the module creates every directory it uses, at import, before any test body runs. So a freshly created empty directory is sufficient: nothing needs to be laid down under it first, and nothing is mounted at /src.

probe.path: /tmp/cwi-fixture-probe.py (the file the two argv lines below mount at /probe.py)
probe.script:
import os, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == "app-first":
    # what the arm-B module run does: tests/conftest.py is imported first
    # (pytest loads it before collecting the module) and it imports api.main.
    import tests.conftest  # noqa: F401  -> sets AITELIER_HOME to its own mkdtemp
    os.environ.setdefault("CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE", tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cwi-"))
    os.environ.setdefault("CODING_WORKSPACE_RAW", os.path.join(os.environ["CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE"], "raw"))
    from tests.integration import test_coding_workspace_integration as m
else:  # module-first: the module imported before anything touched api.dependencies
    os.environ["CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE"] = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cwi-")
    os.environ["CODING_WORKSPACE_RAW"] = os.path.join(os.environ["CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE"], "raw")
    from tests.integration import test_coding_workspace_integration as m
from core import datadir
print("mode                =", mode)
print("CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE =", os.environ["CODING_WORKSPACE_FIXTURE"])
print("module has _HOME    =", getattr(m, "_HOME", None))
print("AITELIER_HOME       =", os.environ.get("AITELIER_HOME"))
print("datadir.aitelier_home =", datadir.aitelier_home())
print("db_path             =", datadir.db_path())
print("semantic_index_dir  =", datadir.semantic_index_control_dir())
print("fixture root existed before? ", "no: mkdtemp made it in this process")
probe.note: the probe only reads os.environ and core.datadir; it writes nothing, which is why the argv carries -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and the tree stays clean.

Fix the stale patch before turning it on: tests/integration/test_coding_workspace_integration.py:766 start_and_die(rid) must accept the host's keyword-only db (def start_and_die(rid, **kw): os._exit(17)) — core/skillflow_host.py:809 start_run(self, run_id: str, *, db: Any = None). That is a test-body change and was out of scope here.

Prefer a per-module fixture root over a tests/conftest.py default: set the two variables in the module (or in tests/integration/conftest.py) so a suite-wide default does not add ~58s and one failure to every default run, and does not leave tests/integration/test_dsh_project_work.py printing a reason that names a variable which is now set.
When that file is next touched, replace its /src capsule probe at :41 the same way (repo root), which is what would actually unskip its 6 class-b rows.

Keep the mkdtemp root out of the committed edit's blast radius: nothing removes it today, so on any runner with a persistent TMPDIR a suite-wide default leaks one directory per session. Under the prescribed `docker run --rm` shape it dies with the container, which is what the arm runs did (HOME=/tmp is the container's own /tmp).
